# Feature: Single-Owner Accounting, Actually On

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-040
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_interaction_wave2_gaps.md`

Close FEAT-034 phase 3. Its TASK-004 and TASK-010 contracts were correct; the migration stopped
short of them, so the runner that owns budgets and the ledger is, in production, **five independent
runners each with its own allowance and its own ledger**, and the verdict data that made
`details.attempted[]` worth reading is thrown away and reconstituted as zeros before the model sees
it.

Three concrete consequences, all measured in run `20260904T001045Z-do-caa285ca` (plan §4, G5–G8):

1. **No shared ceiling.** `runEscalationPlan(plan, parentState?)`
   ([`escalation.ts:218-221`](../../../packages/core/src/interaction/escalation.ts#L218-L221)) and
   `context.runSubplan` ([`:284`](../../../packages/core/src/interaction/escalation.ts#L284)) exist
   and are exercised by exactly one test
   ([`escalation.spec.ts:70`](../../../packages/core/tests/interaction/escalation.spec.ts#L70)).
   **No production call site passes either.** Every nested plan starts a fresh action counter, a
   fresh reacquisition cap and a fresh ledger, so FEAT-034 TASK-010 (iv) — _"`maxActions: 32`
   becomes one real ceiling across the plan and every sub-plan"_ — does not hold at runtime.
2. **The verdict is destroyed in transit.** `toLegacyLedger`
   ([`escalation.ts:341-361`](../../../packages/core/src/interaction/escalation.ts#L341-L361)) drops
   `entryEvidence`, `chargedActions` and `remainingActions`, drops `skipped` verdicts entirely, and
   re-emits `errorCode: null` on success. `toWireAttemptArtifact`
   ([`:369`](../../../packages/core/src/interaction/escalation.ts#L369)) then re-inflates the
   missing fields as `[]` / `0` / `0`
   ([`:684-687`](../../../packages/core/src/interaction/escalation.ts#L684-L687)). Every one of the
   run's 25 ledger records carried `entry_evidence: []`, `charged_actions: 0`,
   `remaining_actions: 0` — roughly 1.5 KB of model-visible noise per failing call, and _"which axis
   spent the budget?"_ unanswerable.
3. **Order is a merge, not a sequence.** `driveFamilyPlan`
   ([`engine.ts:697-709`](../../../packages/core/src/fill/engine.ts#L697-L709)) splices driver-local
   ledgers into the runner's records and renumbers, and its own comment says the migration is
   unfinished. The observable defect: ordinal 1 `driver:combobox` **succeeded** at 9161 ms followed
   by five more rungs, ordinal 6 `query:as-given` **succeeded** at 9159 ms — two records describing
   the same nine seconds at two nesting levels, presented as a sequence. Three further hand-built
   ledgers feed that merge: `queryRecord` / `renumber` in the combobox driver, `enterText`'s
   `retarget-editee` splice, and `probeOpen`'s two-record ledger.

**After this feature:** one `MutableRunState` per top-level fill call. One action ceiling, one
reacquisition cap, one deadline and one ordered sequence of verdicts across every nested plan.
`details.attempted[]` carries the verdict shape FEAT-034 §2 specified — real `entry_evidence`,
`charged_actions`, `remaining_actions`, and **no key whose value is `[]`, `0` or `null`** — with no
projection to a legacy shape and back. `toLegacyLedger`, `queryRecord`, `renumber` and
`WidgetSuccess.attempted` are gone, and `boundary-rules.spec.ts` can see them.

**This changes attribution, not work done.** The 20 gauntlet fixtures keep their pinned
`expectedMutations` and `expectedReads` unchanged — that is the proof. Every budget boundary that
genuinely moves is enumerated one by one in TASK-010, each with its own named test, exactly as
FEAT-034 TASK-010 required.

### What this feature does not do

- **It does not re-specify FEAT-034.** TASK-004's _"the query form travels as the verdict's
  `entryEvidence`"_ and TASK-010's four budget clauses are the contracts being completed, not
  redesigned. Where this spec states a shape, it is FEAT-034 §2's shape unless it says otherwise.
- **G7 is shared, and FEAT-038 owns the larger half.** Terminal unreachable failures answered in
  5.4–6.4 s against a ≤ 4 s target. Plan §4 names G2 — a date-cell label falling through to the
  typeahead path and paying a full reaction settle — as a direct contributor; that is **FEAT-038's
  work and is not implemented here**. FEAT-040 owns making the ceiling real so a nested plan cannot
  restart the allowance, making cost-cap admission bite across nesting, and asserting fast-fail
  end to end on an injected clock (FEAT-034 TASK-012 (c) landed only as a runner unit test,
  [`escalation.spec.ts:173`](../../../packages/core/tests/interaction/escalation.spec.ts#L173)).
- **It adds no capability, tool, flag, preference or dependency** (plan §3, §12 item 4).
- **It does not change any error code, cause, message or hint.** FEAT-032's catalog remains the
  single source of model-visible text.

### The one behavior change the model can see

`details.attempted[]` gains `skipped` verdicts on the fill path (the click path already serializes
them) and loses three always-empty keys. A skipped rung was **not performed**, so
`runtime/profiles.ts`'s standing instruction _"Never repeat anything named in `attempted` — it has
already failed"_ becomes wrong for it and is corrected in TASK-009. That correction is the only
model-facing prose change in this feature.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

> `.spec-lite/data_model.md` does **not** exist, and plan §3 states that every change is in existing
> files with no additions. There are therefore **no tables, no columns, no migrations, no indexes
> and no foreign keys in this feature**. Everything below is a **TypeScript contract shape** inside
> `packages/core` plus the one serialized projection those shapes reach — `details.attempted[]` in a
> tool result and in `tool-calls.jsonl`. FEAT-034 §2 designed these shapes; this section states the
> deltas and the invariants that make them true at runtime.

### Entities & Attributes

**`MutableRunState`** (`escalation.ts:198-210`) — **retained unchanged in shape, given an owner.**
Today it is created inside `runEscalationPlan` and dies with the plan. After this feature exactly
one instance exists per top-level fill call, and it is the single answer to "how much has this call
spent".

- `startedAt`, `deadlineMs`, `maxActions` (`number`) — NOT NULL, immutable for the life of the run.
  Taken from the **first** plan to create the state; a nested plan's own `budget.maxActions` never
  raises or lowers the ceiling (this is TASK-010 (iv) made real).
- `verdicts` (`RungVerdict[]`) — NOT NULL. The **one** ordered sequence. Append-only; `ordinal` is
  assigned `verdicts.length + 1` at push time.
- `values` (`Record<string, unknown>`) — NOT NULL. Accumulated rung evidence, shared across nesting
  so a nested rung's entry condition can read what an enclosing rung produced.
- `chargedActions`, `chargedReads`, `reacquisitions` (`number`) — NOT NULL, monotonically
  non-decreasing for the life of the run.
- `lastOutcome`, `lastFailure`, `lastNow` — NOT NULL (nullable values). Unchanged.

**`PlanBudget.run`** (`escalation.ts:60-66`) — **one new optional field**, and the whole threading
mechanism.

- `run` (`MutableRunState`, optional) — the run this plan joins. Absent means "this plan is the
  root; create the state". Carried on the budget rather than added to every driver signature
  because `WidgetBudget` / `FillBudget` **already flows unchanged** through `fillField` →
  `WidgetDriver.drive` → `commitText` → every plan builder, so threading it changes no public
  signature and stays explicit data rather than an ambient lookup (memory → Architecture: explicit
  dependency injection, no hidden singletons). `runEscalationPlan` resolves the state as
  `parentState ?? plan.budget.run ?? <create root>`.

**`RungVerdict`** (`escalation.ts:158-180`) — **producer contract, unchanged.** Every verdict the
runner emits still carries all measured fields on the `succeeded` and `failed` arms. What changes is
what those fields mean under nesting:

- `chargedActions` becomes **exclusive of nested sub-plan work**. Today a rung that runs a sub-plan
  would report `state.chargedActions - actionsBefore`, which includes its children's charges, so
  summing the ledger double-counts and "which axis spent the budget?" is answered wrongly. After
  this feature the per-rung values **partition** the run total exactly.
- `remainingActions` is the shared remainder at the moment the verdict was recorded, and is
  therefore **monotonically non-increasing down the ledger** — the invariant plan §9 requires.
- `ordinal` is assigned on **completion**, so a nested rung's verdict precedes its enclosing rung's.
  This is the runner's existing behavior, pinned by
  [`escalation.spec.ts:79-80`](../../../packages/core/tests/interaction/escalation.spec.ts#L79-L80)
  (`['child', 'parent']`, ordinals `[1, 2]`), and it is what makes `remainingActions` monotone. It
  is the opposite of today's merge, which inserts nested records **after** their owning rung.

**`RungVerdictProjection`** — **new**, the return type of `normalizeAttemptArtifact`. Identical to
`RungVerdict` except that `entryEvidence`, `chargedActions`, `remainingActions` and `elapsedMs` are
**optional**, because a legacy `AttemptRecord` never carried them and inventing `[]` / `0` / `0` is
the exact defect this feature removes. `RungVerdict` is assignable to `RungVerdictProjection`;
nothing else is.

**`VerdictEvidence`** — **new**, `Readonly<Record<string, string | number | boolean>>`. What a rung
discloses about **how** it resolved, as counts and structural tokens. It replaces the hand-built
`AttemptRecord`s that drivers append today. Constraints, all asserted:

- Values are scalars only. No object, no array, no nested record — a `WidgetContainer.path` or a raw
  candidate list must not be able to reach the wire through it.
- Only keys in `SERIALIZED_EVIDENCE_KEYS` are serialized; anything else stays internal plan
  evidence. This replaces `verdictsToWire`'s current blind `...verdict.evidence` spread
  ([`escalation.ts:389`](../../../packages/core/src/interaction/escalation.ts#L389)), which — once
  the fill path uses `toWireLedger` — would serialize `committed`, `offered`, `chosen`, `editee`
  and `container` verbatim into every successful record.
- No page text. `editee` remains a first-class disclosure on `FillSuccess`, not ledger evidence
  (plan §10: only counts and structural tokens ride the ledger).

**`SERIALIZED_EVIDENCE_KEYS`** — **new**, the declared allowlist, in the spirit of `MAX_OFFERED`
(`combobox-driver.ts:62`) and `MAX_RANKED_OFFERED` (`query-plan.ts:186`):

| Key                     | Type     | Produced by                | Meaning                                             |
| ----------------------- | -------- | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `substituted`           | `number` | FEAT-038's tie-break       | How many candidates were indistinguishable (`>= 2`) |
| `substitution_position` | `number` | FEAT-038's tie-break       | 1-based document-order position taken               |
| `tie_break`             | `string` | FEAT-038's tie-break       | Comma-joined rung names that narrowed the pool      |
| `scroll_steps`          | `number` | `listboxDriver` (FEAT-037) | Bounded container-scroll count                      |
| `scroll_stop`           | `string` | `listboxDriver` (FEAT-037) | Fixed stop reason token                             |
| `revealed_driver`       | `string` | the open probe             | Registry driver **kind** revealed by opening        |
| `reacquisitions`        | `number` | the runner-owned port      | Stale-ref healings charged to this rung             |

**`WidgetSuccess.attempted`** (`widgets/types.ts:187`) — **deleted**, replaced by
`WidgetSuccess.evidence?: VerdictEvidence`. A driver stops owning a ledger; it discloses evidence
and the runner owns records. This is the concrete deletion criterion for G6's "driver-local
ledgers".

**`FillOutcome.attempted`** (`fill/types.ts:103`) — retyped from `readonly AttemptRecord[]` to
`readonly SerializedVerdict[]` (`readonly Record<string, unknown>[]`), i.e. **already the wire
projection**, matching what `browser-fill-element.ts:111` has always declared and what
`browser-click.ts:153` already produces. `strategy` keeps its key name and Wave 1 meaning, so
assertions like
[`fill-engine.spec.ts:306-309`](../../../packages/core/tests/fill/fill-engine.spec.ts#L306-L309)
(`['driver:date-input', 'driver:calendar-grid']`) survive unedited.

**`AttemptRecord` / `AttemptLedger`** (`interaction/types.ts`) — **retained as the legacy read shape
only**, per FEAT-034 and memory's run-artifact compatibility rule. After this feature the only
producers left in `packages/*/src` are `pointer-preflight.ts`'s `clear-obstruction` record (the
controller's own recovery, consumed through `toWireAttemptArtifact` at
[`browser-click.ts:184`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-click.ts#L184)) and
the test fixtures. Every reader still accepts it and **no run directory under `runs/` is rewritten.**

**`MAX_SERIALIZED_VERDICTS`** — **new**, `24`. The serialized ledger is bounded like every other
model-visible list. When a run produces more, the projection keeps the first record and the last
`MAX_SERIALIZED_VERDICTS - 1` — the opening move and the outcome are the two ends a caller needs —
and no record is silently dropped without the bound being observable from the retained ordinals.

### Serialized `details.attempted[]`

FEAT-034 §2's table, with presence made exact. **A key is omitted, never emitted empty.**

| Key                  | Present on                         | Notes                                                        |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ordinal`            | all                                | 1-based across the whole run including every sub-plan        |
| `strategy`           | all                                | `rung.id`, Wave 1 meaning                                    |
| `axis`               | all                                | `where` / `what` / `how`                                     |
| `verdict`            | all                                | `succeeded` / `failed` / `skipped`                           |
| `entry_evidence`     | succeeded, failed — **when known** | bounded structural key list; **omitted when empty**          |
| `charged_actions`    | succeeded, failed — **when known** | exclusive of nested work; **omitted when unknown**           |
| `remaining_actions`  | succeeded, failed — **when known** | **omitted when unknown**; never `0` as a stand-in for absent |
| `elapsed_ms`         | succeeded, failed — **when known** | **omitted when unknown**                                     |
| `error_code`         | **failed only**                    | stable code; **absent**, never `null`, elsewhere             |
| `detail`             | failed, optional                   | one short observed clause                                    |
| `unmet`              | **skipped only**                   | fixed structural vocabulary, no page text                    |
| allowlisted evidence | succeeded, failed — when produced  | `SERIALIZED_EVIDENCE_KEYS` only, scalars only                |

### Relationships

- One **top-level fill call** 1:1 one `MutableRunState` 1:1 one serialized `attempted[]`. Every plan
  executed during that call — the field plan, the driver plan, the combobox plan, the text plan, the
  typing plan, the revealed-driver sub-plan — is N:1 to that state. This 1:1 is the feature.
- One `MutableRunState` 1:N `RungVerdict` by array position; position **is** the ordering, and the
  order is completion order.
- `sum(verdict.chargedActions)` over all `succeeded` and `failed` verdicts **equals**
  `state.chargedActions` (the partition invariant). `skipped` verdicts contribute nothing because
  they spent nothing.
- `state.chargedActions` **equals** the gauntlet counting port's `counts.mutations` for the whole
  call, and `state.chargedReads` equals `counts.reads` — the seam assertion plan §9 requires. This
  holds only because the field port and every rung port charge into the same state exactly once;
  see the idempotence invariant below.
- Legacy `AttemptRecord` 1:1 `RungVerdictProjection` via `normalizeAttemptArtifact`:
  `errorCode === null` → `succeeded`, otherwise → `failed`, measured fields **absent**.
- `toWireAttemptArtifact` is **idempotent** over its own output: feeding a serialized verdict array
  back through it returns the identical array, including allowlisted evidence keys. This is what
  makes the legacy-tolerant boundary safe to leave in place where a legacy producer still exists.

### Indexes & Constraints

- **UNIQUE `Rung.id` within a plan** — unchanged (`assertPlanShape`). Ids repeat **across** plans by
  design: two `overtype` verdicts from two typing plans in one run are two real attempts.
- **Idempotent charging.** Wrapping a port that is already wrapped for the **same** `MutableRunState`
  charges each operation exactly once. Without this, a rung body that hands its own `context.port`
  to a nested plan (which every nested call site does) double-charges every mutation and every read,
  and the seam equality above silently fails. Asserted directly, not inferred.
- **One ceiling.** `state.maxActions` and `state.deadlineMs` are set once by the root and are
  read-only thereafter. A nested plan declaring a different `budget.maxActions` cannot widen or
  narrow them.
- **One reacquisition cap.** `state.reacquisitions` is shared, capped by the root's
  `budget.maxReacquisitions` (4, unchanged). Today the runner's `plan.reacquire` branch is **dead
  code** — no plan sets `reacquire` — and all healing happens in `createRunnerOwnedPort`'s private
  counter, so the cap is per-wrapper rather than per-call.
- **Monotonic remainder.** Across the whole ledger, `remaining_actions` never increases.
- **No always-empty field.** No serialized record contains a key whose value is `[]`, `0` or `null`
  (plan §9). Asserted over a real failing fill, not over a hand-built record.
- **Bounded ledger.** At most `MAX_SERIALIZED_VERDICTS` records reach the model per call.
- **Reader totality.** `normalizeAttemptArtifact` stays total over arbitrary JSON and never throws
  (the existing `fast-check` property at
  [`recovery-characterization.spec.ts:54-60`](../../../packages/core/tests/interaction/recovery-characterization.spec.ts#L54-L60)
  keeps passing).
- **No run-artifact rewrite.** Normalization happens on read only.

## 4. Dependencies

- **FEAT-034 (Recovery as Declarative Data)** — implemented. This feature completes its phase 3;
  its TASK-004 and TASK-010 contracts are reopened, not re-specified (plan §12 item 5).
- **FEAT-032 (Widget Gauntlet)** — the authoritative counting port
  (`tests/support/gauntlet.ts:countingPort`) is the only mutation/read counter this feature asserts
  against. It must not be duplicated.
- **FEAT-037 (Virtualized Lists)** — the counted `scrollContainer` action and the
  `scroll-container` record whose representation changes here.
- **FEAT-038 (Choice Integrity)** — **ordering dependency, row order is dependency order.** FEAT-038
  writes its substitution evidence into the legacy `AttemptRecord.detail` projection and takes the
  gauntlet to 20 fixtures. This feature moves that evidence to verdict evidence (TASK-007) and
  inherits the 20-fixture census. **Do not implement FEAT-038's work here**: the tie-break helper,
  the option-role scoping, the date-family offered-label receiver and the three new fixtures are
  its own. If FEAT-038 has not landed when this feature starts, TASK-007's substitution clause is a
  no-op and the census stays at 17 — state which in the changeset rather than adding fixtures here.
- **FEAT-039 (Fused Field Disclosure)** — no coupling. `browser_fill_form` passes `details.attempted`
  through untouched (`browser-fill-form.ts:165`), and `covers` is orthogonal to the ledger.
- **No dependency on FEAT-035 or FEAT-036.** The delta block and vision are unaffected; the 20

      implementation counts actions, counts reads, and heals stale refs against

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: N/A. No user-facing surface, no CLI flag, no preference, no consent decision. Plan §5
  states the CLI surface is unchanged.
- **Error Handling**: Stable error codes, causes, messages and hints are **unchanged** — this
  feature changes which record carries a code and what accompanies it, never the codes or the
  wording. `classifyFailure`'s `details.reason === 'budget' | 'disabled'` override is preserved
  verbatim, an unrecognised code stays terminal by default, and `browserFailure`'s re-throw of
  unrecognised errors still escapes the runner rather than being retried blindly. The one new
  refusal is `unmet: 'insufficient-remaining-budget'` firing on nested rungs, which is FEAT-034's
  own vocabulary reaching a place a private allowance previously hid.
- **Logging**: The ledger becomes the projection FEAT-034 specified, in the sanitized
  `tool-calls.jsonl` record. `strategy` and `axis` keep their Wave 1 meanings. `entry_evidence` is
  a bounded structural key list, `unmet` a fixed structural vocabulary carrying no page text, and
  serialized rung evidence is restricted to `SERIALIZED_EVIDENCE_KEYS` scalars — counts and
  structural tokens only. Structured Pino logging is unchanged and no new sink is added.
- **Security**: Two concerns, both structural. First, **the evidence allowlist**: switching the fill
  path to `toWireLedger` without it would spread every rung's raw evidence — `committed`, `offered`,
  `chosen`, `editee`, and a `WidgetContainer` path object — into `details.attempted[]`, which is
  unbounded page-derived data in a field that must carry only counts and tokens. TASK-007 lands the
  allowlist **before** TASK-008 flips the path, and that ordering is the mitigation. Second, **the
  secret path is preserved by construction**: `allowEscalation: false` still builds a one-rung plan
  that commits blind, performs no readback, and contributes no evidence to any verdict, so no
  secret-derived value can reach a ledger, a failure detail or a log. Asserted by a dedicated test
  in TASK-004.
- **Dependency direction**: `packages/core` exports the runner, the plan types and the run state;
  `packages/agent` declares the `field` and `click` plans and injects core operations into their rung
  bodies. **`packages/core` never imports `@yantra/agent`**, enforced by the existing
  `boundary-rules.spec.ts` rule and re-verified in TASK-011.
- **Backward compatibility**: `normalizeAttemptArtifact` keeps accepting legacy `AttemptRecord`
  artifacts and stays total over arbitrary JSON. **No existing run directory under `runs/` is ever
  rewritten** — normalization happens on read only, asserted against the checked-in legacy fixture
  whose bytes must not change. User-owned workflow YAML is untouched and the deterministic replay
  path's behavior is unchanged and remains hard zero-LLM.
- **No website-specific logic**: every rung id, entry condition, `unmet` value and evidence key in
  this feature is structural — a registry driver kind, an axis, a query form kind, a count, a
  document-order position. `revealed_driver` names a registry entry, never a page string. A site
  name in any of them is a bug, and `boundary-rules.spec.ts`'s existing rule covers the touched
  modules by path.
- **Testing**: Vitest, AAA behavior tests, injected clocks and ports, mocks only at external
  boundaries; core suites tagged `@no-llm` and run on macOS, Windows and Ubuntu. Targeted runs use
  `cd packages/<pkg> && npx vitest run <path>`, per memory — `pnpm --filter <pkg> test -- <pattern>`
  silently ignores the pattern. `turbo run build` before trusting any `e2e` result about core
  behavior, since `e2e` resolves `@yantra/core` from built `dist/`. Artifact assertions read bytes
  through an explicit UTF-8 decoder.
